ios.desc:
Eintercon – International Chat & Meet People Worldwide

Connect with global friends who share your passions through private, exclusive chat. When you match, you have 48 hours to see if the connection is real. No endless swiping—just genuine bonds across borders.

MEET PEOPLE ACROSS BORDERS

Discover people from around the world based on what you're genuinely passionate about—books, music, travel, hobbies that actually matter to you. Whether you love obscure indie films, quantum physics, or philosophical debates at midnight, you'll meet people who truly get it.

Our smart matching algorithm connects you with compatible global friends internationally, not based on proximity or superficial scores, but on genuine shared interests and passions.

PRIVATE EXCLUSIVE CHAT FOR REAL CONNECTION

Every match gives you access to private, exclusive chat—just you and your connection. Share photos, voice messages, and media in a safe space designed for real conversation. This isn't a public social network with endless feeds. It's your private social network for meaningful international chat with people who matter.

THE 48-HOUR CONNECTION WINDOW

When you match with someone, the clock starts. You have exactly 48 hours for exclusive chat to see if this connection is real. This creates healthy urgency without pressure—enough time for genuine conversation, but short enough that you both stay engaged.

After 48 hours, you both decide together: continue building this friendship or move on to meet people who might be a better fit. No ghosting, no guilt, just honest and respectful clarity.

WHY INTERNATIONAL CHAT & GLOBAL FRIENDS?

Because the best friendships challenge our assumptions. Because someone halfway across the world might understand you better than anyone in your city. Because you can't hate someone whose story you know.

Break out of your local bubble through international chat and discover perspectives you'd never encounter otherwise. Build global friendships that cross continents and change how you see the world.

FEATURES YOU'LL LOVE

• Interest-based matching to meet people worldwide
• International chat with global friends
• Private, exclusive one-on-one messaging
• Real-time chat with typing indicators
• Voice messages for deeper, more natural conversation
• Rich media sharing—photos, videos, voice notes
• 48-hour decision window for every match
• Profile customization with your authentic interests
• Safe, moderated private social network
• No ads, no data sellin

show_hn.title: Show HN: Can 48 hours be enough to form a real connection?

quotes.text:
I built something because I felt lost in the way social media works today. Most platforms reward likes, followers, and numbers. I have over 3,000 connections on LinkedIn, but when I really needed help, I realized I did not know who to turn to. The numbers looked impressive, but the connections felt empty.

That led me to a question: what if connection had a time limit, and it forced us to be more intentional?

So I created Eintercon. Here’s how it works:

You are very unlikely to be paired with someone from your own country.

Instead, you are matched with someone abroad who shares your interests.

You have 48 hours together. After that, the connection expires and you meet someone new.

There are no likes, no follower counts, no endless feeds. Just people, talking to people. My hope is that this time-bound window encourages more genuine exchanges and helps us see the world through each other’s eyes.

I just launched it on the App Store, and I would love your feedback. And here’s something I am especially curious about: if you were to try this, which countries would you be most excited to connect with, and why?

App Store link: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/eintercon/id6749785496

Thanks for reading, and happy to answer questions.

quotes.text:
I’ve been building something I’ve always wished existed: a way to discover and connect with people across the world, but without the endless scroll or shallow matches.

Eintercon is a social app where you get paired with people globally, but each connection lasts only 48 hours. The idea is to give just enough time to have a meaningful exchange before you hop off to meet someone new. It’s not about collecting followers — it’s about sparking real conversations, learning about other cultures, and keeping things fresh.

A couple of things that make it different:

Global-first design: built to make cross-border connections effortless.

48-hour connection window: keeps the experience engaging, without endless ghost chats.

Mailing & Labs: you can also drop into themed chatrooms ("Labs") filled with people from diverse cultures, or send cross-border messages to test how connections spark.

Passport feature: answer light “visa-style” questions to connect intentionally with people from specific regions.

We’re live on iOS (testflight) and web. I’d love feedback on:

Does the 48-hour limit feel like a good balance between fleeting and meaningful?

Are there other cultural-exchange features you’d expect or want in something like this?

Does the name “Eintercon” work for you, or is it too clunky? (I’ve been getting mixed reactions).

quotes.text:
I built something I wish existed when I was trying to make international friends: Eintercon
.

The idea: when you connect with someone new, a 48-hour timer starts. You’ve got that window to chat, exchange stories, or decide if you want to keep the connection alive. If you both agree, the friendship continues. If not, it expires and you move on.

Why this approach?

Traditional apps feel endless, and conversations die quickly.

“Permanent” chats often turn into ghost towns.

But with a deadline, conversations suddenly feel alive and intentional.

It’s not about swiping endlessly, it’s about sparking fast, authentic connections across borders.

We’re live here:

Play Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.eintercon.app

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/ee/app/eintercon/id6749785496

Would love feedback on:

Does the 48-hour concept feel exciting or limiting?

How would you use something like this — casual friends, cultural exchange, learning languages?

What feels missing or off-putting from the early version?

Thanks!
